question: What does the term "Kunbis" refer to in the context of Maratha society?

options.text: A warrior caste of the Rajput clans

solution:
The correct answer is __**A group of peasant-pastoralists**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The term **Kunbis** refers to a significant community in the **Maratha society**, primarily classified as **peasant-pastoralists**. They were traditionally engaged in agriculture and cattle rearing.

• Kunbis formed the backbone of the agricultural economy in the **Deccan region** of India and were closely associated with the rural agrarian structure.

• The Kunbis were considered a part of the **Shudra varna** in the traditional caste hierarchy. However, they played a vital role in the Maratha Empire's socio-economic and political framework.

• During the rise of the Maratha Empire under leaders like **Shivaji Maharaj**, Kunbis often joined the army and became an integral part of the Maratha warrior class. Over time, they were assimilated into the broader Maratha identity.

• Their contributions to agriculture and their service as soldiers in the Maratha army underline their dual role as both **economic producers** and **defenders** of their territories.

• In modern India, Kunbis are recognized as an **Other Backward Class (OBC)** in several states, which provides them with reservations and welfare benefits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Historical Significance of Kunbis:** 

• The Kunbis were primarily farmers in the **Deccan plateau**, which includes regions of present-day Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Madhya Pradesh. Their agricultural practices supported the regional economy.

• They were one of the communities that contributed to the success of the **Maratha Confederacy**, as they provided both agrarian resources and military manpower.

• With the rise of the Maratha power under Shivaji Maharaj, many Kunbis were integrated into the military structure, eventually forming a significant portion of the Maratha warrior class.

• **Kunbis and the Maratha Identity:**

• Over time, the distinction between Kunbis and Marathas blurred as many Kunbis adopted the Maratha identity, particularly those who gained prominence in the military and administration.

• Historical records suggest that the Maratha rulers encouraged this assimilation to strengthen their support base among the agrarian communities.

• The social mobility experienced by Kunbis during the Maratha rule allowed them to rise in social status, although they retained their agricultural roots.

• **Cultural Practices:**

• Kunbis follow a mix of agrarian and pastoral traditions, often celebrating festivals related to harvests such as **Makar Sankranti** and **Ganesh Chaturthi**.

• They have a rich cultural heritage, including folk songs and dances that reflect their agrarian lifestyle and community values.

• **Other Caste Groups in the Context of the Question:**

• **Warrior caste of Rajput clans:** Refers to the Rajputs, known for their martial traditions and ruling dynasties in northern and western India. Not related to the Kunbis.

• **Class of temple priests:** Generally refers to the **Brahmins**, who are traditionally associated with priesthood and religious duties.

• **Community of merchant bankers:** Refers to communities like the **Banias** or **Vaishyas**, known for their roles in trade and finance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Kunbis in Modern India:** 

• In present-day Maharashtra, Kunbis are classified as **OBCs** and benefit from affirmative action policies in education, employment, and political representation.

• They continue to be an important agricultural community, contributing significantly to the rural economy of the state.

• **Role in the Maratha Empire:**

• Kunbis were instrumental in the military campaigns of the Marathas, serving as foot soldiers and cavalrymen.

• Their contribution to the agrarian economy ensured the sustenance of the Maratha state during periods of conflict and expansion.
